title: isolateRealRoots
body:
## isolateRealRoots

Find every real root of one univariate polynomial with exact rational coefficients. SymPy isolates the roots with sympy.intervals(strict=True); the result is a list of disjoint closed rational intervals, each holding exactly one distinct root, with its multiplicity. A rational root is published as an exact point interval. The host then re-proves completeness, disjointness, width and multiplicity from the coefficients alone using a square-free decomposition and Sturm sequences, so a missing or mislabelled root is refused.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Coefficients are literal exact fractions in descending powers; there is no expression syntax, so write x^2 - 2 as ["1", "0", "-2"], including the zero coefficients.
- An interval is not a decimal approximation of the root unless you choose to read it as one; a point interval means the root is exactly that rational number.
- Complex roots are counted but never located, and nothing is claimed about the numerical conditioning of whatever problem produced the coefficients.
- Only SymPy 1.14.0 is accepted; a different release is refused rather than assumed compatible.

Native binding: `sympy.intervals([Poly(list of Rational, x, domain=QQ)], eps=Rational, strict=True)`. Output kind: `["table","text"]`.

Inputs: none.

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `coefficients` | Required list of 2 to 13 exact rational coefficients in descending powers, so the list length is the degree plus one (degree 1 to 12). The first entry multiplies x^degree and must be nonzero; interior zero coefficients are written out ("0"). Each entry is a string of an optional sign, digits and an optional /denominator, at most 40 digits each, for example "-3/2" or "7". Fractions need not be reduced; the plan shows them reduced. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":82},"minItems":2,"maxItems":13}` | **required** |
| `maximumIntervalWidth` | Largest allowed width of each published interval, as an exact positive fraction between 1/10^30 and 1. Narrower intervals take slightly more native work and have longer endpoints. Exact point roots have width zero whatever you choose. The host rejects any interval wider than this. | `{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":82}` | `"1/1000"` |
